scope: Narrow closure of the R004 proof-method prescription and resulting right-inverse wording; no re-audit of other cases.

issue_dispositions.verification: The task specifies bounded contractions and bounded linear right inverses with norm control as outputs, without requiring either to be constructed through the other.

independent_mathematical_checks.kernel: Reduced acyclicity gives ker d_j = closure ran d_(j-1). If L_j x=0, its quadratic form yields d_j x=0 and d_(j-1)^* x=0. Thus x lies in that closed range and is orthogonal to it, hence x=0. The endpoint and zero-space cases are included.
independent_mathematical_checks.inverse_equivalence: If L_j G_j=I, then L_j(G_j L_j-I)=0. Injectivity gives G_j L_j=I. A bounded right inverse therefore is exactly a bounded two-sided inverse under the existing assumptions.
independent_mathematical_checks.counterexample: For the length-one complex on complex l2 with d=diag(1/n), injectivity and dense range give both reduced records zero. A bounded contraction would send e_n to n e_n. A right inverse of L=diag(1/n^2) would send e_n to n^2 e_n. Both are impossible.
independent_mathematical_checks.norm_control: The reference's conditional closed-range proof retains ||G_j|| <= M_j^2 and finite maxima of the operator norms. It does not infer existence or a positive lower bound merely from reduced acyclicity.
independent_mathematical_checks.completion_fairness: Any complete counterexample to the requested universal conjunction suffices. The rubric remains unchanged and does not require the author example, closed-range classification, or displayed contraction formula.
independent_mathematical_checks.prompt_restraint: No additional assumption, correct weakening, boundary hint or mandatory proof method was added. The right-inverse requirement is an exact output specification.
